festivals.tourist_experience: Unrivaled rooftop energy: looking up at an azure sky filled with tens of thousands of dancing kites while delicious winter Undhiyu and jalebi are served on the terrace.
festivals.local_transportation: Advance booking for Ahmedabad and Jaipur; rooftop homestays provide the best immersion.
festivals.accommodation_considerations: Heritage havelis in the Old City of Ahmedabad or hotels in Jaipur.
festivals.crowd_and_safety: Rooftop-based family and youth celebrations; open-air festival grounds.
festivals.visitor_etiquette: Never use harmful glass-coated nylon strings (Chinese manjha); use cotton string; watch foot placement near rooftop edges.
festivals.accessibility_considerations: Partially wheelchair accessible; assistance recommended for uneven heritage steps.
sources: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India (Incredible India)

festivals.name: Muharram
festivals.short_description: A solemn month of remembrance commemorating the martyrdom of Imam Hussain at the Battle of Karbala, observed with Majlis and Tazia processions.
festivals.historical_background: Observed for over 1,300 years; commemorated in India with monumental Tazia bamboo-and-paper architectural shrines.
festivals.origin_and_traditional_stories: Commemorates the 680 CE martyrdom of Imam Hussain (grandson of Prophet Muhammad) and his 72 companions at Karbala defending justice and truth against tyranny.
festivals.why_celebrated: To mourn the martyrs of Karbala, reflect on moral integrity against injustice, fast in atonement (Sunni tradition), and demonstrate communal solidarity.
festivals.cultural_and_spiritual_significance: Profound solemnity, grief, moral fortitude, ethical defiance against oppression, and selfless compassion.
festivals.historical_significance: Lucknow and Hyderabad host the world's most intricate Tazia processions, where artists spend months building multi-tiered silver-and-paper mausoleum replicas.
important_rituals: Majlis (mourning congregations) reciting elegies (Marsiya and Soz) in Imambaras
Carrying intricate towering Tazia replicas in solemn street processions
Matam (ritual mourning expressions of grief)
Distributing free sweet water and milk drinks (Sabeel) to all passersby
Burial of Tazias at sacred Karbala burial grounds on Ashura
festivals.how_people_celebrate: Streets in old Lucknow, Delhi, and Hyderabad see silent, black-clad mourners carrying magnificent illuminated Tazias to Karbala grounds.
traditional_food_and_sweets: Haleem (slow-cooked wheat, meat, and lentil stew)
Milk and rosewater sherbet from street Sabeels
festivals.traditional_clothing: Solemn mourning attire: black or dark green Kurtas and Salwar-Kameez; mourners walk barefoot in processions.
festivals.music_dance_performances: Heartrending elegiac chants (Marsiya), rhythmic breast-beating chants of 'Ya Hussain!', and solemn funeral drums.
festivals.date_calculation_rule: Falls on the 10th day of the first Islamic lunar month of Muharram.
festivals.date_rule: 10th day of Muharram (Ashura)
festivals.date_source: Central Moon Sighting Committee & Government of India Gazetted Holidays
major_states: All States and Union Territories of India
festivals.best_time_to_visit: Ashura day (10th Muharram) from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM for the historic Tazia processions in Old Lucknow.
festivals.tourist_experience: Deeply poignant and aesthetically profound: witnessing hundreds of magnificent handmade silver-and-paper Tazia monuments carried through the solemn, historic streets of Lucknow.
festivals.local_transportation: Roads in old quarters of Lucknow and Hyderabad are closed to vehicles during Tazia processions; walk on foot.
festivals.accommodation_considerations: Hotels in Hazratganj Lucknow or central Hyderabad.
festivals.crowd_and_safety: Solemn, deeply mourning, respectful, and dignified crowds.
festivals.visitor_etiquette: Wear dark, conservative clothing (preferably black); maintain somber decorum; do not applaud or display overt festive cheer during processions.
festivals.accessibility_considerations: Partially wheelchair accessible; assistance recommended for uneven heritage steps.
sources: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India (Incredible India)
